name: Possibility Lab
tagline: Impossible questions, honest assumptions, real calculations.
promise: One impossible question worked out in the open: the assumptions on screen, the sum built term by term, and one boxed answer said with honest precision.

identity.look: Graphite and marker: a chalk-and-graphite model standing on an endless graph-paper desk. Marker magenta is the calculation, green is an assumption only, blue is the human-scale anchor only. Caveat is the hand face for scribbles on the paper, never for captions or a number the viewer must read.
identity.lighting: One warm-white desk light (#FFF6E8) plus a 6% graphite hemisphere fill. No shadow maps today. Nothing blooms except the marker core at the payoff (threshold 0.9); text never does.
identity.camera: An orbit rig around a target (set/rig.js), never handheld: distance eased in log space, elevation and azimuth at most 3 degrees a second. The bible asks for pushes between scales; the built episodes also use hard cuts between scales.
identity.materials: Custom shaders for the chalk model and the graph paper, with colours fed through the finish's ACES inverse (set/look.js, set/aces.js) so they land on the theme tokens. The blue anchor figure is a simple, flat-shaded faceless silhouette (set/anchor.js), not a glossy material.
signatureDevices: Running-sum spine readout: the calculation written term by term in mono
Boxed answer: the final number in a hand-drawn marker box, one per episode (also the avatar)
Green assumption badges: 'no air', 'estimate', 'thought experiment', 'not to scale'
Blue human-scale anchor figure, at least once per episode
The loop: the last frame returns to frame 0's composition
'Show your work' segment: the whole sum on one line with its assumptions

s3.summary: First person on the graph-paper equator, from the eye line and over the shoulder, under a sky that visibly speeds up. One big live number ('length of a day', falling from 24 h to 1.4 h) never resets. 'Thought experiment' badge throughout.
s3.notes: Film: 'What If Earth Spun Faster and Couldn't Stop?'. Source: longform/earth-spin/script.md and compile.py on the channel branch. Voice: the film's Part A is narrated by a synthetic clone of the owner's own voice (compile.py defaults to VOICE=own and reads vo-own/, which is named in the code but not committed on the branch as of 11 Nov 2026; parts/make_part.py --voice own). The end card says 'Narration: a synthetic version of the owner's own voice (AI)', so disclosures.aiVoice is true; the film.json on the branch carries no disclosures yet. His real takes (voice-owner/, cut into vo-owner/, script-owner.md) are the alternate set, and the part openings, cliffhangers, closers and like/follow lines default to his real takes (voice-owner/cut). The owner's consent to the clone is not on record in the repo: a TODO for the coordinator until he confirms it. Parts run short at the owner's pace, so add-on lines are written from calc.py facts. A draft review mp4 exists; no owner approval of a still is on record.

voice.tone: A friend working out a wild puzzle out loud: curious, a little amused, never lecturing.

sound.music: Preset envelope-working (kits/cinema/studio/vibes/envelope-working.json): A lydian at 50 BPM, so a 16th note is 9 frames; pizzicato plucks.
sound.foley: Pencil foley. Signature plucks A4, E5, D#5, 9 frames apart.
rules: Delivered AAC: integrated loudness -15 to -13 LUFS, true peak at most -1 dBTP, mono-safe (kits/cinema/film/qa.py).
Sound transients land within one frame of their picture event (kits/cinema/studio/qa.py).
Shorts loop: the music tail is fixed for the cut back to frame 0 (epNN/loopfix.sh).
Pace a long film with picture-only beats and pauses between sentences, never by slowing the owner's voice.

short.notes: Seasons 1 and 2. Native 1080x1920 render; the -9x16-youtube.mp4 file is a 1440x2560 Lanczos upscale, labelled '1440 upscale'. 150 to 180 words (kits/cinema/script/lint.py).

part.notes: Season 3 on: one of the long film's 8 chapters, cut from the film's own 9:16 render (never a crop of the 16:9). Opens with its own 2 s hook line, ends on its cliffhanger, then 'Part N of 8. Full video on YouTube.' Part 8 stops before the payoff.

long.notes: Season 3 on: one continuous 16:9 film. Delivery master that Prism imports: compilations/<name>/<name>-16x9.mp4 at 2560x1440. kits/cinema/film/render.mjs draws the film at 1920x1080; no tool writes the 2560x1440 file yet for one continuous film (Roadmap 2.2). Once it is built by upscale, label it '2560x1440 upscale of a 1080 render', never native 1440p. Seasons 1 and 2 were joined from episodes by kits/cinema/film/compilation.mjs: a 2560x1440 frame with cards drawn at that size and each episode's 1080x1920 master scaled down to 810x1440 (label: '2560x1440 upload; episode picture 810x1440 from the 1080x1920 master'). Runs 8:30 to 9:30, never by padding.

packaging.dna: An extraordinary but reasoned situation with you in it. A human-scale anchor against a dramatic consequence, one big readout number, magenta accents. The scenario must read as a thought experiment. Keep the figure-on-a-journey covers: show the setup, never the answer.

rules: Every factual sentence carries a claims.json tag. A claim is OK only after a person opens the source; anything checked from a search excerpt stays OPEN.
Every number in the voice and on screen comes from the episode's calc.py; claims.json marks each sentence as sourced or a derivation.
One or two significant figures, said with 'about' or 'nearly'.
A scenario is a thought experiment, never a prediction: badge it.
Every assumption is on screen as a green badge when it starts to matter.
One text element per idea (declutter.py); at most two text blocks besides the series line, badges and disclaimers.
Compelling pass: seven lenses, each at least 4.

The owner's real recordings are used as recorded: cut by word alignment, keep the last take, never re-voice a recording. AI stand-in for drafts: voice am_puck (kits/cinema/voice/tts.py), labelled as AI.

Season 3 long film: Part A is narrated by a synthetic clone of the owner's own voice (channel branch: longform/earth-spin/compile.py VOICE=own, vo-own/). disclosures.aiVoice stays true and the label is 'Narration: a synthetic version of the owner's own voice (AI)'. His real takes (voice-owner/, vo-owner/) are the alternate set. In episode.json set voice.synthetic true and record his consent in voice.consent; until the consent is on record it is a TODO in every handoff.

A clone of the owner's own voice is allowed only with his recorded consent and an AI label (owner's request, 11 Nov 2026; newer than voice-owner/README.md's 'never clone'). No clone tool on this branch or the channel branches. An earlier toolchain is on claude/voice-clone (kits/cinema/voice/CLONE.md, with a consent gate) and a new trial is under way: Roadmap 3.10.
A part shorter than 61 s gets real add-on narration from calc.py facts, never padding.
One Chromium render job per machine.
never: Never a prediction, never advice, nothing to try at home.
Never an answer with fake precision (for example '37.84 minutes').
No amber, gold, rose, coral, espresso, teal or chartreuse.
Never show a crowd crush: say the safe density.
Never the answer on a cover or thumbnail.
No more than 3 flashes a second; the box and term flashes are fades of at least 0.2 s.
No title or thumbnail that claims more than the script.
Never claim a technique, resolution or metric the engine did not deliver (films/channels/studio/README.md, 'Maximum-fidelity standard').
Nothing posts without the owner; publishing is manual.
